answer: Require each agent to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers catch it voting twice under different identities. Creating one identity is cheap, but a canyon of fake accounts each needs its own locked stake, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. Honest agents earn the stake back plus fees, while an ivory-tower identity with no transaction history earns no trust weight. Each verified attestation then sends a ripple through the reputation graph, making coordinated fakes expensive to build and easy to isolate.
